author: Loren Tate
title: Illinois Freshman Keaton Wagler's Stellar Performance Leads to Victory Over Purdue
text:
• Illinois guard Keaton Wagler scored 46 points against Purdue, the second-highest in Illinois history.
• Illinois defeated Purdue 88-82 at Mackey Arena.
• This was Illinois' 13th win in their last 50 trips to West Lafayette.
• Purdue's Braden Smith scored 27 points and had 12 assists.
• Wagler made 9 of 11 three-point attempts.
• Wagler is projected to move up in NBA mock drafts.
• Illinois made four consecutive three-pointers in the second half.
• The article references a temporary restraining order involving Alabama player Charles Bediako, who signed an NBA two-way contract after leaving Alabama in the 2023 NBA draft.
• The ruling could allow players to return to college after receiving partial pay from an NBA team.
• Players like James Nnaji, Landon Johnson, and Abdullah Ahmed, who entered the NBA draft but did not receive a salary, are also mentioned.
• The article discusses the potential impact on college basketball if players can earn more money in college than in the G League.
summary: After missing a sixth free throw of the second half, the Illini roared from a 73-69 deficit with four straight three-pointers, two by Tomislav Ivisic and one each by Jake Davis and David Mirkovic. But this had it all: An underdog setting with Illinois senior Kylan Boswell missing, a raucous environment, and an Illini team seeking its ninth straight win and a spot in the Top 10. It’s labeled as “could be’ because Tuscaloosa County Circuit Judge Jim Roberts (a six-figure donor to the Crimson Tide) handed down a restraining order that is temporary, and could be soon overturned.
